citations.title: Statistics Exercise Guide
citations.text:
Problem 3: Confidence Interval for a Mean
Question. A sample of n = 36 students has mean study time 12.4 hours per week. The population standard deviation is known to be 3 hours. Build a 95% confidence interval.
Solution. The standard error is 3 / sqrt(36) = 0.5. The margin of error is 1.96 * 0.5 = 0.98. The interval is 12.4 plus or minus 0.98, that is (11.42, 13.38). Interpretation: the procedure captures the true mean in about 95% of repeated samples. If the sample size were four times larger (n = 144) the standard error would halve to 0.25 and the interval would become narrower.

When sigma is unknown and n is small, replace 1.96 with a critical value from the t distribution with n - 1 degrees of freedom. A 95% confidence level means that if the procedure were repeated many times, about 95% of the intervals would contain the true parameter; it does not mean there is a 95% probability that one specific computed interval contains it.

S5.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S5.text: 4. Sampling and Confidence Intervals A population is the entire group of interest and a sample is a subset used to learn about it. Simple random sampling gives every member an equal chance of selection; stratified sampling samples within subgroups; convenience sampling is easy but prone to bias. Sampling bias occurs when the sample systematically differs from the population. The sampling distribution of the mean describes how sample means vary from sample to sample. The Central Limit Theorem states that for sufficiently large n the distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal with mean mu and standard error sigma / sqrt(n), regardless of the shape of the original population.
